draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Mapusa! Its Municipal Market, built in 1960, was the first planned market in Goa and now has more than a thousand shops. Come on a Friday and the famous Friday Market runs from early morning to late evening.
draft.hungryLine: Mapusa is the place for traditional Goan food, cooked both Catholic and Hindu style, and for cold kokum juice by the taxi stand.

moodReplies.show-me-around: The Mapusa Municipal Market is a 7 minute walk, and St. Jerome Church, with its shrine of Our Lady of Miracles, is about 14 minutes away.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Browse the off-the-beaten-track shelves at the Other India Bookstore, or catch a Konkani play at Hanuman Natyagraha.
moodReplies.surprise-me: St. Xavier's College here is the largest and oldest college in Goa.

legends.title: A feast for everyone
legends.body: The feast of Our Lady of Miracles draws thousands of devotees every year. Locals see it as an example of Catholic and Hindu amity.

tips.title: Go on a Friday.
tips.body: The weekly Friday Market runs from early morning till late evening.

tips.title: Take home a plant.
tips.body: Buy a plant or tree at the Friday Market and help keep Goa green.

story.title: Mapuçá
story.body: Under Portuguese rule the town was known as Mapuçá. It grew into the headquarters of Bardez taluka.

story.title: A school is born
story.body: The Saraswat Education Society founded Saraswat Vidyalaya as a Marathi primary school in March 1911.

story.title: St. Britto's
story.body: The Jesuits founded St. Britto High School for boys in Mapusa in 1946.

story.title: Goa's first planned market
story.body: The Mapusa Municipal Market was built in 1960, the first planned market in Goa.

story.title: North Goa's shopping town
story.body: Mapusa is the main commercial centre of North Goa, and its Friday Market draws more tourists every year.
